structuredExplanation.whatIf: If the selected index changed, the verified statement would change to the option at that corresponding position. If the option order changed, the index would refer to the newly positioned option.
structuredExplanation.keywords: reviewer verification; single-choice question; selected option index 0; first listed option
structuredExplanation.whyCorrect: The verified answer identifies selectedOptionIndexes as [0]. With zero-based indexing, index 0 refers to the first listed option, so that is the statement verified by the reviewer.
structuredExplanation.generalRule: When an answer key supplies an option index, interpret it using zero-based indexing unless the instructions specify otherwise: 0 means the first option, 1 means the second, and so on.
structuredExplanation.commonMistakes: Confusing zero-based and one-based indexing, selecting the second option because it appears later, or treating generic option wording as stronger evidence than the reviewer-approved selection.
structuredExplanation.eliminationStrategy: Use the reviewer-provided selection as authoritative. In a single-choice item, retain the option at the specified index and eliminate the remaining option(s).

warnings: The option wording is generic, so the reviewer’s selected position is the decisive evidence.
